messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw an alert storm during the last small canary roll (5% traffic). Lots of p95 alerts across many routes even though absolute error counts were tiny. Wondering if our current guards are too noisy for low-traffic slices.

Priya: Yup — this is expected when we compare canary -> baseline without accounting for sample size. Right now alerts use percent-diff only, so a jump from 10ms->20ms at 10 reqs/s looks the same as 10ms->20ms at 1k reqs/s.

Jorge: We should treat traffic slices as separate cohorts and include both absolute and statistical significance checks. Propose adding min_sample_count + weighted-delta logic to guards.

Lin: On the dashboard side, we can add a "slice compare" widget that shows baseline vs slice p50/p95, qps, error-rate, and sample counts. Also add a visual tag when sample_count < suppression_threshold (greyed out).

Samira: Telemetry note — we need to surface per-slice QPS and per-token cost too. Right now cost is aggregated which hides canary economics. If a canary is very cheap but shows high p95 variance, teams might ignore it.

Alex: Agreed. Can we sketch a minimal rollout guard config that would stop the noisy alerts? Something like min_samples + absolute_delta + relative_delta?

Jorge: Example proto config below — very lightweight, backwards compatible with existing guards:

```json
{
  "rollout": {
    "id": "r-1234",
    "traffic_split": {"baseline":95, "canary":5},
    "guards": [
      {"metric":"p95_latency_ms","absolute_delta_ms":50,"relative_delta_pct":0.2,"min_sample_count":500,"window":"5m"},
      {"metric":"error_rate","relative_delta_pct":0.1,"min_sample_count":200}
    ]
  }
}
```

Priya: +1. Also add a suppression rule: if sample_count < min_sample_count then suppress alerts and mark the slice as "insufficient data" in UI. That avoids noise and makes it explicit to teams.

Lin: For the dashboard UX: add these controls — "min sample threshold" per-metric, toggle to show weighted vs unweighted diff, and an inline link to open the exact query used for the comparison (for debugging).

Samira: For telemetry pipeline, we should tag metrics by rollout_id and slice_id so the drilldown can reconstruct which requests were canary vs baseline. This avoids heuristics based on header sampling.

Alex: What about alerting semantics? I think we should require BOTH: 1) relative delta > X AND 2) absolute delta > Y OR p-value < 0.05. Plus min_samples. That should cut false positives.

Jorge: I prefer Bayesian intervals instead of p-values for stability. Compute a 90% credible interval on the difference; alert if the lower bound > 0 (or whatever delta). More stable with low counts.

Priya: Either approach works but we must keep compute cost low — we run this for many rollouts. Maybe run a fast approximate bootstrap for high-QPS slices and a simple threshold for low-QPS.

Lin: Quick alert config sketch for ops to consider:

```
alert:
  - name: canary-p95-regression
    when: (delta(p95) > 0.20) AND (qps_baseline > 100)
    suppress_if: (sample_count_canary < 500)
    notify: [#oncall, #prod-alerts]
```

Samira: We should also add a metric that reports "alerted-slices" per rollout so we can track alert fatigue and tune global defaults.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Canary r-1234 incremented to 5% at 2026-03-09T15:12:08Z — image: inference:v2.8

Alex: Action items:
- Priya: prototype guard semantics + suppression logic (min_samples + weighted delta) — owner: @Priya
- Jorge: implement Bayesian/approx bootstrap option in the stats lib and expose a fast path — owner: @Jorge
- Lin: mockups for "slice compare" dashboard widget + sample_count visual state — owner: @Lin
- Samira: ensure rollout_id/slice_id propagation in telemetry and add per-slice cost metric — owner: @Samira
- Alex: write short RFC for rollout observability defaults and alert semantics — owner: @Alex

Priya: I'll put a small prototype in a sandbox this week and link screenshots. Expect a simple demo with synthetic traffic.

Jorge: I'll pair with Priya on the sampling heuristics.

Lin: I'll draft the widget and share in #design-review tomorrow.

Samira: Will check telemetry schema and open tickets for tagging.

Alex: Great. If anyone wants to re-open the convo, ping me. For now let's aim to ship suppression + dashboard tile before the next canary wave. :thumbsup:
